title: Latent circuit inference from heterogeneous neural responses during cognitive tasks
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Infer a compact recurrent circuit accounting for the original two-monkey PFC condition-averaged responses and native context-dependent task output, retaining all 72 stimulus/context conditions.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Infer a compact recurrent circuit accounting for the original two-monkey PFC condition-averaged responses and native context-dependent task output, retaining all 72 stimulus/context conditions.

Source-paper comparison for Original monkey-specific projected test R-squared with total-variance capture and native task-output fit retained: Paper reports projected test R-squared, but equations 31-32 print normalized norm-based error terms and the released diagnostic helper uses a different variance normalization. Recover exact centering, squaring and conversion to reported R-squared; a standard formula cannot be assumed.
success_criteria: Recover the original empirical census, half-trial protocol, timing adapter, objective, projection and reported-score formula. Historical membership is acceptable, but documented source-conformant stochastic half-trial reruns are also admissible when the original protocol/population, calibration tolerance and paired candidate-author comparison are preserved.

Retain both monkeys and every original eligible unit/condition. The candidate must surpass the source-paper result itself for each monkey (reported A 0.88 and F 0.76) at recovered source precision under a predeclared justified stochastic-calibration tolerance, as well as show paired improvement over the calibrated author baseline on matched half-trial realizations. A weaker author rerun cannot lower the source target or make a candidate below the source result a paper win; merely reporting proximity to the published anchors is insufficient.
Predeclare meaningful improvement and uncertainty while retaining captured-variance and native continuous task-output safeguards; increasing fit in an easier learned projection alone is insufficient.

Preserve the complete 200-initialization-per-monkey reference and original selection policy, including failed starts, using documented source-conformant seeds/reruns where historical seeds are unavailable; do not confuse all-fit score aggregation with top-ten connectivity summaries.
Treat fixed-original-neuron loss, new nested or condition-blocked splits and binary choice accuracy as separately labelled extensions; none is interchangeable with published projected R-squared.
Larger inferred suppression or smaller Mann-Whitney p-values cannot constitute method-performance improvement.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
